extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, and IP professionals filing patent applications in Singapore (IPOS users)
extracted.subtask_description: Formal requirements and procedural standards for preparing and filing patent applications (including PCT national phase) at the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS), covering specification, claims, drawings, abstract, sequence listings, forms, priority claims, corrections, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete application contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete application for a patent contains: (a) A request for grant of a patent, accompanied by the prescribed fee; (b) A description of the invention (should describe at least one way of carrying out the invention claimed, with examples where appropriate, and with reference to the drawings, if any); (c) One or more claim(s) (the claims define the scope of protection and should be supported by the description); (d) Any drawing(s) referred to in the description or any claim(s); (e) An abstract of the invention (summary used in publication of the patent application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference: Section 25 and 2.1.1. All items must be attached in the Specifications tab when filing (2.3.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for grant must be on Patents Form 1
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for grant of a patent must be made on Patents Form 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For securing a date of filing an alternative document 'indicating that a patent is sought' may be submitted, but Patents Form 1 and filing fee must follow within one month or the application will be treated as abandoned (2.1.2–2.1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of filing criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Date of filing is the earliest date on which the documents filed satisfy: (a) indicate that a patent is sought; (b) identify the applicant; and (c) contain something which is or appears to be a description of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When these requirements are complied with, a notification of date of filing will be issued; if Form 1 and fees were not submitted, they must be submitted within one month to complete the application (2.2.12–2.2.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and presentation of the description
rubrics_metrics.description: The description should commence with a title (same as on Patents Form 1) and shall: (a) Specify the technical field; (b) Indicate the background art useful for understanding/searching/examination; (c) Disclose the invention so that the technical problem and its solution can be understood and state advantageous effects; (d) Briefly describe figures; (e) Set forth at least one mode for carrying out the invention, with examples where appropriate and with reference to drawings; (f) Indicate explicitly, where not otherwise obvious, the way(s) in which the invention is industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description may contain chemical/mathematical formula or tables but should not contain drawings, flow sheets or diagrams; pages should be consecutively numbered in Arabic numerals (2.2.1–2.2.4). See Rule 23 for more presentation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: structure and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims define the matter for which protection is sought and shall be in terms of the technical features of the invention (expressed in structural, functional or mathematical terms). Claims shall be written either: (a) in two parts (first part indicating features that are part of prior art; second part introduced by words like 'characterised in that' followed by features defining the invention), or (b) in a single statement reciting a combination of elements or steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should be supported by the description (2.2.7–2.2.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims presentation and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should commence on a new sheet of paper placed after the description to form one set of documents. If more than one claim, claims should be numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: description pages 1–10, claims begin on page 11. Follow Rule 23 for presentation (2.2.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims should not rely on description or drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall not rely, in respect of the technical features of the invention, on references to the description or drawings, unless such a reference is necessary for understanding of the claim or enhances clarity/conciseness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid incorporating material by reference unless necessary (Rule 19(9), 2.2.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for furnishing claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are not required at time of filing to obtain a date of filing; the applicant shall submit the claims to the Registry within 12 months from the date of filing if there is no declared priority date, or within 12 months from the declared priority date, or 2 months from lodgement date for divisional applications. The time period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit claims within the specified time results in abandonment of the application (2.2.10–2.2.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of claims and excess-claim fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to keep the number of claims reasonable. Claims in excess of 20 attract a fee per claim at the search and/or examination phase and for issuance of certificate of grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be strategic about claim drafting to avoid additional fees (2.2.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and presentation of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be submitted as a separate set of documents commencing on a fresh sheet; each drawing/figure should be clearly numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals (independent of sheet numbering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings generally must be black, white or grayscale (no colour), should not contain textual matters, and features should be denoted by reference signs mentioned in the description or claims. Drawings should be scalable so that reduction to 2/3 keeps details distinguishable (2.2.14–2.2.17). See Rules 21 and 23 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: form, length and figure indication
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract is a separate document forming the same series as the description and claims, placed immediately after the claims. It must be as concise as the disclosure permits and normally not contain more than 150 words. If the specification contains drawings, the applicant must indicate on the abstract the figure intended to be published (up to two figures), or indicate 'No Figure'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications lodged on/after 14 Feb 2014 the abstract no longer needs to commence with a title. The text of the abstract must be identical between the attached document and the abstract text field in Patents Form 1; where chemical/mathematical formula or tables cannot be captured, enter 'Refer to abstract attached' (2.2.18–2.2.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing formalities and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application discloses a sequence, the description must include a sequence listing presented as a separate part and in a manner complying with IPOS Digital Hub Practice Direction No. 2 of 2023; for filings on/after 1 Jul 2022 sequence listings shall comply with WIPO ST.26. Any sequence listing not included in the description on the date of filing does not form part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings intended to form part of the description should be attached using document type 'sequence listing (specification)'; sequence listings submitted only for search use 'sequence listing (for reference)' accompanied by a declaration. Non-compliant sequence listings may be later resubmitted in compliant form and incorporated by amendment/correction with accompanying statements and cover letters (2.2.26–2.2.39).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements required for sequence listing amendment or correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific declaration statements must accompany sequence listing submissions: (a) For an amendment under Rule 48: a declaration that the amendments do not include matter beyond the disclosure in the application as filed; (b) For a correction under Rule 91: a declaration that the corrections are what was originally intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adding or correcting sequence listings after filing, use Patents Form 13/13A or Form CM4 as appropriate, and explain changes and basis in a cover letter (2.2.30–2.2.33).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of missing or non-compliant sequence listing on search
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sequence listing forming part of the description is not provided or not provided in the prescribed manner, the Patent Examiner need only search the application to the extent that a meaningful search may be carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More details in the Examination Guidelines for Patent Applications (2.2.34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing formats and size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent specifications may be filed in DOCX (Microsoft Word) or PDF; DOCX is the preferred format. The size of each uploaded document cannot exceed 100 MB; documents exceeding 100 MB must be split into parts not exceeding 100 MB each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than three parts are needed, contact IPOS for splitting guidance (2.3.3–2.3.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of invention requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title is a formal requirement and must be short, precise and indicate the matter to which the invention relates. The Registrar may reframe the title if it fails to comply. Because the title will be published, avoid disclosing too many details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can edit auto-populated titles when claiming an earlier filing date; changes may be made by Patent Examiners during search/examination (2.3.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority claims to earlier filings in Paris Convention/WTO member countries may be made provided the Singapore application is made within 12 months from the earlier filing date. A declaration must be made indicating date and country of each earlier application; the earlier application number, if available, should be provided and must be furnished before 16 months from declared priority date if not available at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration of priority and late addition/correction of priority are possible by following specified forms and time limits (2.3.9–2.3.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language/translation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Formalities officer considers filed documents to be in a language other than English, the applicant will be notified to provide an English translation and Verification of English Translation (VET) within 2 months from notification; failure to comply will result in refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely provision of translations is mandatory for non-English documents (2.2.40).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure prior to filing and novelty impact
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention may be considered not new if already made available to the public—such disclosure may destroy novelty and be grounds for revocation. There are rules (including limited exceptions for certain exhibitions and grace period provisions) governing when prior disclosure may be disregarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed before/after certain dates different provisions apply; see Chapters 6.1.18–6.1.24 for current grace period rules (2.2.41–2.2.44).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of errors — forms, types and required information
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to correct errors on Patents forms, register entries, specifications, or any other document relating to a patent must indicate the source of the error and use the correct correction type on Form CM4 (e.g., 'Correction of Form', 'Correction of Register of Patents', 'Correction of Specification of a Patent or of an Application for a Patent', or 'Correction of any other document relating to a Patent or Application for a Patent'). The request should provide details to be corrected and the relevant Patents rule(s) (Rules 58 and/or 91).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 23 Jul 2018 Form CM4 is used; from 18 May 2018 applicants should indicate the relevant rule(s). For non-form documents the request must be accompanied by marked-up and clean copies of proposed correction (11.8.6–11.8.13, 11.8.22–11.8.23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for allowing correction of a specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections to a specification (Rule 91 standard) shall be made only where the correction is obvious in the sense that it is immediately evident that nothing else would have been intended than what is offered as the correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must include supporting reasons/documents; Registrar may call for written explanations or evidence to satisfy that there is an error (11.8.16–11.8.18, 11.8.23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections affecting published applications/third parties — exceptional grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests under Rule 91 to correct declared priority information in a published patent application will only be allowed under exceptional grounds. IPOS will consider non-exhaustive factors such as: (a) Impact/effect on rights/interests of third parties; (b) Nature of the error (e.g., clerical); (c) Whether the error is obvious or readily apparent on the face of the published application or other documents; (d) Time lapse between publication and request and reasons for delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should put forward reasons/evidence in a cover letter; Rule 58A may require advertisement of corrections under certain conditions (11.8.20–11.8.21, 11.8.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrar's power to advertise correction requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Registrar determines that the interests of any person may be affected by certain correction requests under Rule 58 (from 26 May 2022), the Registrar may advertise the proposed correction by publishing the request and nature of the proposed correction in the Patents Journal. The Registrar may also advertise proposed corrections under Rule 91.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising applies to errors in names or particulars in the register or information pertaining to a priority application; this may affect processing time (11.8.14–11.8.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marked-up vs clean copies and claim corrections after Dec 2019
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting correction of a specification or making corrections to claims, the request shall be accompanied by both marked-up and clean copies of the proposed correction. From 1 Dec 2019, if corrections have been made to claims, a marked-up copy and a clean copy of the full set of claims must be submitted, and amendments/corrections should be reflected similarly in both copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Chapter 5.1.12 for accepted formats of marked-up and clean copies (11.8.13, 11.8.25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct form mapping for common procedural requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The manual lists which form to use for common purposes (e.g., appoint/change/remove an agent: Form CM1; amendment of address for service: Form CM2; correction of applicant/inventor’s name: Form CM4; amendment of specification: Patents Form 13; addition or correction of declared priority date within 16 months: Patents Form 57; transfers: Form CM8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correct form to avoid processing delays; see the table in 11.8.12 for mapping (11.8.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of register entries by Registrar
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registrar may correct any entry in the register which is attributable wholly or in part to an error, default or omission on the part of the Registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar may require evidence/supporting documents and may perform correction subject to Rule 58(4) (11.8.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and numbering of sequence listing in filing (for certain filing dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications with date of filing from 26 May 2022 to 30 Jun 2022: if sequence listing is intended to form part of the description, it must be placed immediately after the description and before the claims and be numbered independently from the description and claims; the page count for each item must be indicated under the checklist in Patents Form 1 and the sequence listing page count included in the page count for the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new document type 'sequence listing (specification)' exists for attaching sequence listings to Patents Form 1 (2.2.36–2.2.38).
